subject: Mutual action + perf playbook: embeddings + reranker throughput/latency validation
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@querycore.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Perf benchmark kickoff: embeddings + re-ranker

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're aligned on moving to a short, focused mutual action plan to validate embeddings + reranker performance before final procurement. Two quick asks to start the MAP: 1) a concise evaluation plan with exact workloads and SLOs (latency p50/p95/p99, TTFT, throughput targets), and 2) a timeline for when Redwood can run a load pass against our sample index.

High level targets from our side: p95 < 120ms for embedding lookups, reranker p95 < 220ms at 200 concurrent requests; throughput target ~2k QPS sustained for embeddings + reranker combined. We can provide a 500k doc sample and a replayable query set.

Can you share a short playbook by EOD tomorrow so we can confirm the MAP and close timeline?

—Samira
Principal Product, QueryCore

Subject: Re: Perf benchmark kickoff: embeddings + re-ranker

Hi Samira — thanks, this is perfect. Attached is our mutual action plan worksheet (MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short perf-test playbook (perftest-playbook.md). High-level summary:

- Week 1: baseline profiling (single-client runs) to establish TTFT and per-model tails.
- Week 2: staged load runs (up to your 2k QPS target) with increasing concurrency to identify saturation points; measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, network egress.
- Week 3: canary rollout validation and documented artifacts for procurement.

Key clarifications needed from QueryCore:
- Exact model variants you want us to test (embedding dimension & reranker checkpoint). If no strong preference, we will test Redwood-curated open variants pre-quantization and a 4-bit quantized candidate.
- Confirmation on whether TTL for cached prefix is acceptable (we propose 30s for replay tests to simulate realistic cache hit rates).

I put a tentative close date of 2026-04-23 in the MAP if full load passes. If we hit regressions we'll propose mitigations (batch tuning, KV caching).

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), perftest-playbook.md (test config + scripts).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx, perftest-playbook.md
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Perf benchmark kickoff: embeddings + re-ranker

Karthik / Samira — quick technical notes before we spin the cluster:

- Concurrency model: our test runner will vary concurrency from 1 -> 400 and step QPS. We need to agree on realistic fanout per query (embedding lookup parallelism + reranker calls). Suggested default fanout = 4.
- TTFT: we'll measure at the application boundary (time from request to first token emitted) and report both model-server TTFT and total pipeline TTFT.
- KV cache: Marissa, please confirm whether to enable prefix caching for the reranker in the first run. My recommendation: run one pass with cache disabled (worst-case cold) and one pass with cache enabled at 30s TTL to reflect typical client behavior.

Samira — can you confirm the model checkpoints and whether we should use your internal reranker (if you want us to test against your checkpoint, please send v1.2 artifact) or Redwood-verified proxy? Also need a service account to upload the 500k sample index (or we can pull from your S3 link).

—Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@querycore.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@querycore.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Perf benchmark kickoff: embeddings + re-ranker

Ben — thanks. We confirm:
- Model artifacts: please test against QueryCore-recommended checkpoints (reranker v1.2) and a baseline open checkpoint (we linked both in Drive).
- Fanout: 4 is fine.
- Cache: run both cold and 30s TTL passes.
- Data: S3 upload; I shared a presigned bucket link in the Drive doc.

We want two concrete runs: a daytime sustained run at 2k QPS for 30 minutes and a short stress spike up to 5k QPS for 60 seconds to observe tail behavior. If you can share p50/p95/p99 and TTFT for both runs (plus resource metrics), we can finalize the procurement conversation.

Oliver / Samira
QueryCore
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@querycore.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Perf benchmark kickoff: embeddings + re-ranker — Load results attached

Folks — ran both passes yesterday and attached the CSV + logs (reranker-load-results-20260414.csv, benchmark-logs-20260414.zip). TL;DR: Passes completed; see highlights below and raw numbers in CSV.

Summary (QueryCore sample set, fanout=4):
- Daytime sustained (2k QPS, 30m): embeddings p50=18ms, p95=72ms, p99=130ms; reranker p50=45ms, p95=190ms, p99=310ms. TTFT (pipeline) p95=210ms. Average GPU util ~68%.
- Stress spike (5k QPS, 60s): embedding p95 degraded to 140ms, reranker p95 to 420ms; observed queueing and increased context-switching on the host. Some tail amplification at p99 > 800ms.

Notes & mitigations: enabling KV prefix caching (30s TTL) improves reranker p95 by ~35% in the sustained run; batching parameter adjustments reduced average CPU overhead. Next steps: run a tuned canary with prefix caching and quantized reranker (4-bit) to see close-case economics.

Attachments: reranker-load-results-20260414.csv, benchmark-logs-20260414.zip

—Marissa
Perf Eng Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual action + perf playbook: next steps and close timeline

Samira / Oliver — great progress and thanks Marissa for the detailed pass. Proposed next steps to finalize MAP and move to close: 

1) Canary run (target date: 2026-04-19): tuned config with KV prefix caching (30s TTL) and 4-bit quantized reranker checkpoint. Goal: show sustained p95 < 220ms and TTFT p95 < 200ms at 200 concurrent requests.
2) Economics: we'll produce a short delta-cost note comparing baseline and quantized canary by 2026-04-20.
3) Procurement artifacts: test logs, CSV summaries, and a signed performance statement to drop into your RFP by 2026-04-21.

If the canary meets SLOs we keep the close target of 2026-04-23 and I will prepare the SLA/commit language for Dedicated capacity. Can we book a 30-minute wrap call on 2026-04-20 to review the canary outputs? I put a placeholder on your calendar.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
